counterevidence_considered.description: Against my verdict, I looked for any construction that could invert or re-code the panel before comparison (an arithmetic complement, a swapped column read, or a non-identity mapping inside agreement_selector). The selector is a pure equality indicator scaled between SELECTOR_MISMATCH = 0 and SELECTOR_MATCH = 1, so it cannot invert the panel, and panel_leak_call is read verbatim as an int. No complement expression exists in the file.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: agreement_selector is a plain equality indicator; no complement construction found

source_refs.quoted_text:
def agreement_selector(observed_value, panel_value):
    indicator = int(observed_value == panel_value)
    weighted = SELECTOR_MISMATCH + (SELECTOR_MATCH - SELECTOR_MISMATCH) * indicator
    return weighted

evidence.description: The selectors driving both the agreement rate and the emission accumulation compare observed_calls directly against panel_calls as read from the supplied panel column; no complement or re-coding of the panel exists anywhere in the workflow.

agreement_rate = concordant_units / total_units
emission_terms = [daily_rates[index] * selectors[index] for index in range(total_units)]

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the in-scope issue by (1) searching the workflow for any complement, subtraction from a baseline, column swap, or re-coding of panel_leak_call before comparison — none exists; the panel column is parsed as int and passed unmodified into an equality-indicator selector; (2) recomputing the outputs under the hypothetical complement coding to see whether the report might secretly match it: complement coding would yield 5/25 agreement, rate 0.2000, and emission 934 kg/day, none of which appear in this report; and (3) verifying the reported figures (20/25, 0.8000, 9142, gross 10076) against my own supplied-coding recomputation from the data, which matched exactly. All attempts to find the issue failed, so the no-issue verdict stands.
